mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where real GDP increased for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% over the last two months signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as supply-side growth supports corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increased by more than 1% over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 10% over the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where housing starts decreased by more than 10% over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate further rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3% within the last month, it signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increased by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.3% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP and a simultaneous decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% within the last month signal strong economic fundamentals, which typically lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as both supply and demand-side indicators align positively.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where real GDP increased and the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.3% within the last month.
